title: La Purísima
goal: Sing at a door on the 7th of December and get sweets for it
culture: The seventh of December. Somebody shouts the question at a door, everybody within earshot shouts the answer, and the house hands out la gorra — sweets, sugar cane, fruit, a whistle. It is the most Nicaraguan night of the year and you do it with somebody who knows the houses.

beats.es: El siete gritamos en las puertas. Yo pregunto y usted contesta. ¿Quién causa tanta alegría?
beats.good: One question, one answer, at every door in the country on the same night. It is the one call and response you cannot afford not to know.

beats.es: ¡Eso! Y entonces le dan la gorra.
beats.good: La gorra is what the house hands you at the door: sweets, fruit, a stick of sugar cane, a plastic whistle. Everybody goes home with a bagful.

beats.es: Dulces, caña, un pito. Y usted grita otra cosa cuando se la dan.
beats.good: Shouted, on somebody’s doorstep, by grown adults. It is not a joke and by the fourth house you will be shouting it too.

beats.en: Alright then. I’ll come with you.
beats.good: Going with somebody who knows which houses give what is the only way to do your first Gritería. Going alone is carol singing without the carols.
